examples._description: mast3r — best quality, slowest. Uses deep feature matching + GLOMAP mapper.
fastmap — fast SIFT features + FastMap mapper. Good default for most scenes.
colmap — SIFT features + COLMAP incremental mapper. More reliable than fastmap on tricky scenes.
hloc — SuperPoint + LightGlue features + COLMAP mapper. Best balance of speed and quality for low-texture/metallic scenes.
pycusfm — GPU-accelerated SIFT features + GPU matching + pycolmap mapper. Fast on large frame sets.
2dgs — 2D Gaussian Splatting trainer. Better surface geometry than Brush. Uses same COLMAP data layout.

argument_reference.video_url: URL to the input video (HTTP/HTTPS or Google Drive share link). Required.
argument_reference.sfm_backend: SfM backend to use: mast3r | fastmap | colmap | hloc | pycusfm. Default: mast3r
argument_reference.trainer: Training backend: brush (default) | 3dgut | 2dgs. 3DGUT skips undistortion and handles camera distortion natively. 2DGS produces sharper surface geometry.
argument_reference.fps: Frames per second to extract from the video. Default: 2
argument_reference.iterations: Number of Brush training steps. Default: 7000 (use 30000 for higher quality)
argument_reference.max_resolution: Max image dimension (pixels) passed to Brush trainer. Default: 1920
argument_reference.oversample: Extract fps*oversample frames then keep the sharpest per window. Default: 3
argument_reference.window_size: [mast3r only] Sliding-window pair size for MASt3R matching. Default: 10
argument_reference.match_overlap: [fastmap | colmap | hloc only] COLMAP sequential matching overlap. Default: 5
